finding.shortLabel: Analysis: an all-movable estate with no valued real estate
finding.statement: The 1663 appraisal is essentially all personalty because John held no valued real estate at death: his principal Braintree farm was the leased Tyng tenancy he never owned, the one freehold he had held outright (the Monatiquot house and orchard) he had sold to Richard Thayer in February 1661/2, and his sole land entry — the Quinapaug interest — was an unpriced frontier share the appraisers 'know not.' The £55 14s 6d therefore measures his movable estate alone.

incoming.explanation: Cross-unit: the colonial John's 1663 estate inventory is the primary record fixing his own death timing against which the 1662 London hearth-tax entry is read as incompatible.

outgoing.explanation: The itemized appraisal values (horse, oxen, swine, young cattle, plough-gear, grain) are the direct arithmetic basis for the livestock/husbandry-dominant profile.
The itemized household goods (apparel, bedding, small pewter/brass, one cupboard, chair/frame, barrels, trays, musket) are the direct basis for the sparse-household reading.
The full inventory line-scan showing no tailoring tool or cloth is the evidentiary basis for the occupational negative.
The inventory carries only movable goods plus one unvalued land line, directly grounding the all-personalty reading of the £55 14s 6d total.

finding.statement: The manuscript inventory of John Gurney Senr's goods and estate, Braintree, 16 March 1663 (taken by Gregory Belcher, Edmund Quincy, and Thomas Faxon), itemizes his movable estate line by line — apparel, boots and hat; bedding, blanket, pillows and cases; pewter, pincers, brass skillet and kettle; a cupboard and a musket; plough-irons, coulter, axes, mattock and chisel; a chair and frame goods, barrels and trays; wheat and Indian corn with grain-boxes, hoops and tubs; a horse and yoke of oxen; sows, pigs and young cattle; an old barrow, wheels and axletree; and one unvalued land line 'an estate layd out in land at Quinapaug wch we know not' — appraised in all at £55 14s 6d.
